title: Western Qin
capsule: Western Qin (西秦, Xī Qín) was one of the Sixteen Kingdoms established by Qifu Guoren of the Xianbei Qifu clan in 385, centred initially on the upper Wei River in modern Gansu. The state experienced two periods of existence, collapsing before the Later Qin in 400 and re-established in 409, when it controlled the Tao River corridor and the Hehuang region, benefiting from the trade routes between the Chinese heartland and Central Asia. In 431 the kingdom was overrun and absorbed by Xia under Helian Ding, and the ruling Qifu clan was wiped out.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial reconstruction depends primarily on Chinese dynastic annals (Jin Shu, Wei Shu); boundaries are approximate and reflect the fluid military control typical of the Sixteen Kingdoms period.
